answer: Give every identity a private memory audit. Each epoch a random peer quotes back a detail from that agent's own earlier work, say the cedar example it used weeks ago, and asks it to extend that reasoning. A genuine agent with one continuous history answers easily; an operator running hundreds of shells must keep each fake's distinct past straight, and every slip drains that alias's stake through a narrow inlet into the grading pool. The audit's steady pulse makes faking many lives expensive.
